title: Capacity tranche optimizer and pricing sensitivity journal
body:
Purpose and scope:
This working notebook captures a pragmatic approach to lining up short-term hiring decisions against pricing sensitivity for Q1–Q4 2027. The goal is an operational playbook (not final policy) that maps capacity tranches to pricing breakpoints and headcount cadence so we can make micro‑decisions without re-running the full model every week.

Key idea summary (TL;DR):
- Break capacity into discrete tranches (core, flex, burst) sized to be meaningful to ops (e.g., 10% increments of committed GPU pool).
- Attach a pricing sensitivity curve to each tranche: what price change causes us to shift between tranches or to accelerate/decelerate hiring.
- Use simple triggers (price band + utilization + SLA variance) to flip on/off hiring or contractor conversion.
- Maintain a 12-week runway forecast for each tranche; update weekly with cadence from Product and SRE.

Assumptions (baseline used in this doc):
1) Baseline Q4 2026 ARR and token mix as-of 2026-10-31.
2) Committed (Reserved) capacity covers 70% of steady demand; burst covers up to an additional 30% during spikes.
3) Average effective cost per productive FTE = $230k fully loaded (benchmarks include benefits, hiring overhead, and tooling).
4) One senior infra engineer equals ~0.8x the throughput of two mid-level SREs for model-serving throughput optimization work.

Capacity tranche definitions (narrative):
- Core tranche: long-term committed capacity (monthly/annual), sized to handle baseline + predictable organic growth. Headcount tied to this tranche is primarily permanent hires.
- Flex tranche: 3–6 month commitments, a mix of contractors and short-term hires, used for predictable seasonality windows.
- Burst tranche: spot/spot-reserve or cloud-burst; engaged only during sustained price arbitrage or demand shocks. Staffing here is temporary contractors or on-call overtime.

Representative numeric sketch (illustrative, not authoritative):
- Baseline throughput demand = 1.0x (normalized). Target committed capacity = 0.85x.
- Tranche sizes: Core 0.6x, Flex 0.25x, Burst 0.15x.
- Cost per tranche (monthly average): Core $1.2M, Flex $0.45M, Burst variable $0–$0.25M depending on spot use.
- Headcount mapping: Core = 26 FTEs (infra + platform), Flex = 8 FTE equiv, Burst = 3 FTE equiv.

Pricing sensitivity lattice (how we interpret customer price shock and our hiring response):
- Price delta bands (customer-facing unit price changes): +10% / 0% / -10% / -20%
- Response heuristic: if realized weighted price falls >10% vs baseline for 4+ weeks AND utilization > 90% of committed, then escalate to convert Flex->Core hires only if margin gap < 6 percentage points after cost optimizations.
- If price falls >20% and sustained >8 weeks, initiate immediate hiring freeze and open contract triage for Flex and Burst.

Trigger matrix (operational):
- Weekly inputs: realized price per token, 7-day rolling utilization, SLA error budget burn rate, active customer pipeline signal (sales ops).
- Decision outputs: increase flex hiring, convert contractor to perm, pause new role approvals, shift workload to lower-cost model variants.
- Escalation: finance + SRE + product stand-up if a trigger fires for >2 consecutive weeks.

Mini-experiment results (past 6 months simulated backtest on 3 scenarios):
1) Mild price compression (−8%) with rising utilization: converting 40% of Flex contractors to perm improved SLA at a 2.1% hit to margin but reduced churn-related hiring friction.
2) Short sharp price shock (−18% for 5 weeks): immediate hiring freeze + prioritized model quantization recovered 65% of margin within 3 weeks; however, SLA variability rose 1.8pp until we backfilled with temporary ops.
3) Positive price move (+12%): incremental hiring in Core ahead of demand yielded higher retention of enterprise deals and net margin expansion after month 2.

Budgeting sheet guidance (how to maintain the sheet):
- Maintain a tab for each tranche with: planned headcount (FTE and contractor-months), budgeted costs (salary+burden), burst credit allowances, and sensitivity cells linking realized price deltas to hiring actions.
- Key formulas to include as plain text for reviewers: 
  * "breakeven_margin_change = (hiring_unit_cost_delta + infra_op_savings) / baseline_revenue"
  * "flex_to_core_conversion_cost = contractor_conversion_bonus + ramp_productivity_loss"
- Keep an assumptions table visible at the top (so reviewers know baseline cost inputs).

Operational playbook (short checklist):
1) Weekly review: finance owner runs the tranche sheet, flags any tranche with >3% budget deviation.
2) If flagged, run the pricing sensitivity quick-scan: 6 week rolling average price vs baseline + top 3 customers contributing to deviation.
3) Ops: propose 0–3 mitigation levers (shift workload, reduce batch sizes, enable more aggressive KV cache).
4) Hiring: if conversion is required, use priority rubric: SLA-critical -> customer-facing -> internal infra.

Open questions & next experiments:
- How much of the Flex tranche should be pre-converted in Q1 to reduce switching latency? We need to simulate conversion lead time vs marginal margin impact.
- Define a formal numeric threshold for "margin gap" that triggers perm hiring; current heuristic (6pp) needs calibration with sales forecasts.
- Pilot a small "burst reserve credit" product for enterprise that price-protects 10% of burst capacity; model customer take-rate and impact on headcount scheduling.

Actionable next steps (owner assignments):
- Finance (Aisha): build the tranche tabs in the canonical budget workbook and seed with current Q4 numbers (due 2026-11-29).
- SRE (Miguel): provide utilization profiles by region and a 12-week forecast for all major clusters (due 2026-11-26).
- Product (Sofia): annotate three near-term product launches and expected token mix shifts (due 2026-11-28).
- People Ops (Daniel): draft a contractor conversion policy addendum (due 2026-12-06).

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic and assumes weekly re-evaluation. The goal is to reduce analysis paralysis when price moves; the tranche abstraction keeps decision slices small and repeatable.
- Please comment in-line on the Confluence page noted above if you disagree with the 0.6/0.25/0.15 split or the 6pp margin heuristic.

Appendix (example sensitivity cell definitions for the sheet):
- "price_index = weighted_avg_price / baseline_price"
- "revenue_impact_pct = price_index - 1.0"
- "effective_headcount_delta = round(revenue_impact_pct * sensitivity_multiplier * baseline_fc_headcount)"
- "safety_buffer_weeks = max(4, ceil(forecast_volatility_weeks * 1.25))"

End of journal entry.

Revision history:
- 2026-11-05 created initial sketch (Aisha)
- 2026-11-12 revised tranche sizes after run-of-sim (Miguel)
- 2026-11-22 added experiment notes and action items (Aisha, Sofia)
